## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- Instructions or demonstrations in the prompt can change model behavior. Few-shot prompting uses a handful of examples to show the desired transformation.
- This operates during inference by changing the context the prediction is conditioned on. Fine-tuning adjusts parameters beforehand.
- RAG may retrieve external documents and insert them into the context. The model can use them when they are supplied.
- Zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot mean zero, one or a few task examples. These terms describe what the prompt supplies and do not identify the internal mechanism producing the behavior.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

Adding two classification examples to a prompt improves its answers. Which parameters were learned at that point?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

The addition updated no model parameters. The new examples changed the context and therefore the distribution of answers.

</details>
